title: Creating Custom Annotations
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of creating custom annotations using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates creating custom annotations.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Creating Custom Annotations** as part of **Annotations, Reflection, and Code Generation**. Annotations and code-generation tools add metadata or generated code; reflection has runtime/tooling costs and Kotlin reflection/JVM APIs have their own maturity considerations. Use the subtopics—Annotation Classes, Annotation Parameters, Documenting Annotation Contracts—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.title: How to reason about it
content_blocks.text: Start with annotation classes. Then compare it with annotation parameters. Identify the input, state, dependency, or branch that determines the result. The snippet is a static reference for CodeLeaf and is not executed in the lesson page.

items.title: Annotation Classes
items.text: Annotation Classes should support a clear object invariant: make valid states easy to represent, restrict mutation to the intended API, and keep initialization and dependencies explicit.

items.title: Annotation Parameters
items.text: Annotation Parameters describes how behavior is declared, passed, or composed. Make inputs and return types clear, keep side effects visible, and use a small call-site example to judge readability.

items.title: Documenting Annotation Contracts
items.text: Documenting Annotation Contracts is one part of creating custom annotations. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset
content_blocks.text: If the example fails, first confirm which runtime/project type the snippet requires. Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
